text:
jen-support: FYI customer (AcmeInc) reporting intermittent 502/504s against hosted inference during high-throughput streaming. They provided curl + trace ids. Happening ~every 10-20s for a few minutes then clears. Repro steps in thread.

aaron-sre: can you paste the trace ids and a sample request? we need trace -> envoy/ingress logs. suspect ingress upstream churn or retry storm.

jen-support: trace: trace=tx-8a3f2f,tx-8a3f30, sample curl: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d @input.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream` . Customer says errors only when payloads are large (10-30KB) and when they concurrently open ~40 streams.

maria-runtime: thanks. two quick questions: 1) is this occurring across regions or just eu1? 2) any recent ingress/NGINX or auth service deploys?

jen-support: only us-east for this customer. they claim it started ~2 hours after a config rollout. no major model swap reported.

chris-ng: I pulled ingress controller events for the time window — saw a burst of upstream 5xx from `auth-cache` and `frontdoor` backend. NGINX logged several `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)`. looks like keepalive pool exhaustion causing resets, then client retries, then backpressure (spiral retries).

aaron-sre: spiral retries = retry loop where client-library retries + ingress retries amplify. if upstream resets mid-stream, envoys/NGINX try again and hit same exhausted pool. we should: 1) throttle client retries, 2) limit ingress retry count for streaming, 3) check `keepalive_requests`/`keepalive_timeout` mismatch.

devops-oncall: ran `kubectl exec -n ingress -c nginx nginx-pod -- cat /var/log/nginx/error.log | tail -n 200` and grabbed a short snippet:
```
2026/03/20 14:02:12 [error] 12345#0: *987654 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.11.12.13, server: api.redwood.ai, request: \"POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\", upstream: \"http://10.2.3.8:8080/\", host: \"api.redwood.ai\"
2026/03/20 14:02:13 [crit] 12345#0: *987660 upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream
```

maria-runtime: "upstream sent too big header" is interesting — could be our auth header or billing meta from downstream is large. also large payloads + many concurrent streams could cause buffer pressure. can we get the exact header sizes from customer's sample?

jen-support: customer sample shows `X-Customer-Meta: {long json blob ~3.2KB}` and `Authorization` normal. they said they added extra billing metadata yesterday.

chris-ng: that explains `too big header`. NGINX default `proxy_buffer_size` and `proxy_busy_buffers_size` can trip. two paths: quick mitigation increase buffer sizes in ingress (hot patch to the ConfigMap for the nginx ingress controller) OR strip/limit incoming `X-Customer-Meta` at the edge (short-term).

aaron-sre: for immediate mitigation: 1) add ingress annotation to temporarily increase `proxy-buffer-size` and `proxy-busy-buffers-size`, 2) set `proxy-next-upstream` to avoid retrying on `error` for streaming path, 3) add a rate-limit on concurrent streams for that tenant. I can push an emergency ingress patch if ops approves.

devops-oncall: prepared a small patch: `nginx-controller-config: proxy_buffer_size: 16k, proxy_busy_buffers_size: 64k` and set `proxy_next_upstream: off` for `location /v1/stream`. staged to one node for canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started: nginx-config-canary -> ingress/nginx-controller (pod/ingress-nginx-7c9f) at 2026-03-20T14:08:04Z

jen-support: rolling now. customer on standby for verification. they will run same repro.

maria-runtime: long-term fixes: 1) add validation on gateway to reject overly large `X-Customer-Meta` with 4xx and guidance to customers, 2) add header-logging to trace header size spikes, 3) consider streaming path bypassing some buffering (proxy_buffering off) when upstream supports chunked streaming.

chris-ng: also add a circuit-breaker on upstream connections `max_conns` per host to avoid pool exhaustion and configure ingress `keepalive` to match upstream services (auth/cache/frontdoor).

devops-oncall: canary looks good on node-1, no regression. logs show reduced `too big header` errors for the canary.

jen-support: customer ran their load and reports 95% success now, small tails still fail occasionally. they throttled concurrent streams to 25 and errors dropped.

aaron-sre: ok follow-ups: - escalate to runtime to add `proxy_buffering off` experiment for /v1/stream - add header-length metric and alert - add tenant limit on concurrent streams in gateway rules - document recommended max header/metadata size in API docs

maria-runtime: scheduling a post-mortem with infra + product to define header limits and default ingress tuning. I'm adding a ticket: RW-ENG-5421.

jen-support: I'll update the customer and keep thread open until full resolution. thanks all :thumbsup:

chris-ng: quick note for the runbook: when you see `upstream sent too big header` + `prematurely closed connection` on streaming paths, check (1) header size, (2) proxy buffer sizes, (3) concurrent stream counts, (4) retry amplification. those four catch most of these.

devops-oncall: recording timeline and attaching logs to ticket RW-ENG-5421.

jen-support: closing loop: customer confirmed stable after ingress patch + temporary tenant throttling. leaving follow-up tasks in RW-ENG-5421 for next week.
